initial.prompt:
Duck Rails low-poly 3D game-render concept, simple flat-faced polygon geometry and clearly pixelated low-resolution textures on broad surfaces. Teal hull, ivory cockpit frame, amber rail trim and lights, warm wood deck, charcoal machinery. No avatars, bags, crates, coal bins, decorative coal, rear crossrail, or pendant lamp. All five views depict ONE unchanged train, not variants. Reference 1 supplies plan layout ONLY; reference 2 overrides furnace appearance: tall thick stack, real hollow mouth with little particle fire at back. Reference 3 supplies centered EMPTY chair and exact dashboard controls. Reference 4 supplies approved plain speaker-only teal receiver and separate angular mic with amber base TALK button. Do not copy its old short furnace. Create a high resolution landscape technical turnaround board with FIVE large isolated train renders arranged with clear white labels on charcoal neutral background: FRONT, BACK, RIGHT SIDE, TOP (FRONT LEFT), REAR-RIGHT THREE-QUARTER. No atlas on this board; atlas delivered separately. Use disciplined consistent object placement across all five cameras. Header 'DUCK RAILS / TRAIN TURNAROUND'. Simple neutral studio lighting, legible dark recesses, minimal smoke to avoid hiding geometry. No scenery.

LOCKED SPATIAL MODEL, NEVER MOVE OR MIRROR PROPS: train deck 10m along longitudinal Z, 5m across X. FRONT is +Z, rear -Z; driver's left is negative X. Front small cockpit roof ONLY covers Z+3 to+5. Driver chair center X=0,Z+3.7 faces front +Z. Dashboard ahead Z+4.6, throttle X=0, fuel gauge X=-0.8 DRIVER LEFT, horn X=+0.8 DRIVER RIGHT. Headlight outside nose at X0,Z5. Two cockpit side lamps only. Furnace body center X=-1.5,Z+1.9 (LEFT SIDE just BEHIND/OUTSIDE cockpit), body 1.6m long x1.6m wide x1.4m tall, charcoal hollow cube; large square open mouth faces toward deck center (+X), all other sides solid. One thick square vertical stack directly atop that furnace, approx2.1m high above casing (total3.5m above deck), clearly taller than cockpit roof, outside roof. Radio table center X+1.9,Z+2.1 on RIGHT SIDE, opposite furnace, outside cockpit. Teal receiver facing inward (-X); microphone at table's aft end. Rear two thirds empty. Continuous low side rail interrupted by centered boarding gaps Z-1 to+1 BOTH SIDES. REAR ENTIRE WIDTH OPEN, no bar or gate across back, flat unobstructed deck edge. Only FOUR simple wheels total, one front and rear axle, maintain positions Z+3.8 and-3.8 in every view. Keep train shell, chair, controls, table station and furnace visibly distinct modules.

CAMERA-SPECIFIC PROJECTION CHECKS:
FRONT facing nose from +Z: furnace and tall stack are on IMAGE RIGHT behind cockpit; radio on IMAGE LEFT behind cockpit, possibly partly hidden. Center headlight and chair aligned. This is narrow frontal elevation.
BACK looking forward from -Z: furnace on IMAGE LEFT, radio IMAGE RIGHT, clear rear boarding edge with NO railing, centered chair beyond them. Stack left, NEVER right. Radio speaker faces inward.
RIGHT SIDE camera from +X: nose FRONT at IMAGE LEFT, rear at IMAGE RIGHT. Near-side radio immediately behind cockpit at left-third. Far-side furnace at SAME longitudinal station behind cockpit, partially occluded by near-side table, its very tall stack visible. One stack only. Middle boarding gap, no rear bags.
TOP camera looking down, FRONT at IMAGE LEFT: furnace on BOTTOM side immediately right of cockpit; radio on TOP side at same station; empty chair centered halfway between upper/lower edges; dashboard ahead left of chair, horn above throttle, fuel below throttle. Show roof as thin outline/cutaway ONLY IN TOP so seat is visible. Stack directly on furnace. Open rear edge at image right.
REAR-RIGHT THREE-QUARTER camera from +X,-Z elevated: open rear foreground, cockpit in distance; furnace on far/left side of deck, radio nearer/right side. Furnace hollow inward face visible across deck. Tall stack at same side as furnace. Radio receiver's BACK is visible because camera is on its outer/right side; do not spin radio to show grille. Preserve all placements and roof. Big center empty aisle.

Use coherent same geometry, same height, same 4-wheel scheme and same prop positions. No exploded view, no bonus props, no reversed captions, no model sheet sketch. Each required view must be shown once, full train and stack uncut. Make top and side views wide, front/back narrower.

Generate a square flat UNLIT pixel-art texture atlas for Duck Rails low-poly train, based on attached style references. This is a proposed color atlas for later UV mapping, NOT a 3D render. Edge-to-edge square atlas, exactly 4 columns x4 rows of equal square tiles. No labels, text, borders, lighting, shadows, perspective or objects. Crisp chunky visible pixel blocks, restrained 4-6 colors per tile, consistent pixel scale. Every tile should fill its square with subtle tiled material variation. ORDER row1 left-right: weathered dark teal painted steel; ivory painted trim; muted amber painted metal; near-black chassis steel. Row2: warm brown wooden deck plank texture; charcoal furnace exterior; dark sooty inner firebox walls; black rubber seat material. Row3: teal radio casing; ivory speaker grille with repeated dark square pixel holes; dull gray exposed metal; dark brown table wood. Row4: warm offwhite lamp lens color texture (flat no baked glow); red horn cap color texture; dark gray control panel background; neutral midgray trim metal. Surfaces use broad pixel patches and limited localized wear matching DuckZ style, no photorealism. No baked flames/smoke or bright orange fire tile: those are separate particle effects. No faux knobs or modeled shapes. No UV wireframes. Clean aligned 4x4 tile atlas, no gaps between cells. High-resolution output with deliberately low-resolution pixel motif, use nearest-neighbor style crisp edges.

refinements.prompt:
Correct this Duck Rails five-view turnaround sheet while preserving its layout, titles, train shape, style, coloring, roof, headlight, empty deck, open rear, sideboard gaps, wheels and existing prop sides. Reference 2 specifies actual hollow furnace mouth appearance. Treat all panels as one fixed assembly. Perform these exact corrections:
1 FRONT panel upper-left: dashboard gauges and horn should face the driver toward rear, not toward exterior camera. Replace visible three-control FRONT faces with a plain dark teal dashboard BACK slab, keep empty chair centered behind it. On radio at imageleft show appropriate end view, not turn it toward camera. Furnace on imageright stays.
2 BACK panel upper-middle: looking from train rear, furnace at IMAGE LEFT presents solid AFT face, not its coal mouth. Make this face a solid charcoal surface. Mouth only exists on inward face toward train center, which is its narrow right-hand face in this projection. Preserve radio on IMAGE RIGHT, centered chair and controls visible beyond. One furnace only.
3 RIGHT SIDE upperright: radio table currently too far aft. Slide entire near-side table/radio/mic LEFT toward nose so its center is at EXACT SAME longitudinal station as furnace center, immediately outside roof. This table will OCCLUDE lower portion of far-side furnace; respect overlap! Tall stack remains visible above and behind table. Show radio's PLAIN TEAL BACK to this camera, no cream speaker grille, since speaker faces inward away from right-side viewer. Do not show furnace fire through table or receiver. Side boarding gap remains centered behind both stations.
4 TOP lowerleft: empty seat and center throttle must be centered halfway across train width, slide them toward imagebottom if needed. Horn toward imageupper, fuel toward imagelower. Keep radio on upper side and furnace lower side at same longitudinal station. Top view is roof cutaway, no added objects. Keep rear edge open.
5 REAR-RIGHT THREEQUARTER lowerright: keep furnace left and radio right; align radio table opposite furnace, same longitudinal station just behind cockpit, not farther aft. Enlarge the furnace's inward-facing open mouth to roughly65% of its face width and60% of height; visible dark HOLLOW INTERIOR with inner floor and walls and a few tiny particle flames at back, never a solid orange panel. Mouth faces the radio across aisle. Keep radio teal back facing camera, grille away. One furnace and one table total.
Maintain same taller stack proportions across FRONT BACK SIDE and THREEQUARTER, straight dark thick shaft above furnace, total height about1.7 times cockpit roof height. No humans, cargo, added lights, rear railing, duplicate controls or duplicate furnaces. Five original labeled angles all preserved. Make corrections clean and coherent; this is same model seen from different cameras.

Edit ONLY the small dashboard controls and microphone placement in this train turnaround. Preserve ALL other geometry, materials, labels, viewpoints, furnace, radio receiver and table, centered empty seat, roof, side gaps and open rear. The second reference is the authoritative dashboard: LEFT square fuel gauge, CENTER tall black throttle lever, RIGHT small RED SQUARE HORN PUSHBUTTON with a white horn icon printed flat. NEVER depict a trumpet or brass horn object! Exactly 3 controls. Correct BACK panel: square gauge on imageleft, black lever imagecenter, small red square button imageright. Correct REAR-RIGHT THREEQUARTER: same driver-relative arrangement, gauge left, levermiddle, redbuttonright; no brass trumpet. Correct TOP panel (front left): horn red square button goes ABOVE throttle, tall black throttle in MIDDLE directly ahead of seat center, square gauge BELOW throttle. No round extra dials. FRONT panel keeps plain dashboard BACK and must NOT show controls. RIGHT SIDE control detail can stay mostly occluded.
Microphone station consistency: mic is on table INBOARD edge directly alongside receiver at SAME longitudinal Z station, not at either fore/aft end. TOP panel: mic/base goes directly BELOW the teal receiver toward deck center, not to its left. RIGHT SIDE panel: mic now behind receiver from camera, remove the currently visible mic to right of receiver, allow just small mic tip above receiver center. BACK panel: mic is just LEFT of receiver at inner table edge, not right. THREEQUARTER: mic mostly occluded by receiver but small tip allowed on its inward edge. Keep same angular mic and one amber TALK base button. Do not move the table or receiver. Keep whole sheet same layout, no added panels. No other changes.

limits: Generated concept views, not measured projections from a common mesh. Atlas is proposed color/material tiles, not UV-bound or a finished game texture; final UVs, padding, power-of-two resolution, mip behavior, decals and masks require authoring and validation.
